utterances.text: I don't recall if they did. It's probably unlikely, but I don't recall how they moved back and forth to each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did Serbian civilians move along the straight line, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My memory is pretty foggy on this one, but there were some movement across the airport that was controlled by the UN. I just can't remember what the details of the moment across the airport were for the people there. It's been too long.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: General, with another witness here, with Mr. David Harland -- I'm sure that name rings a bell. He was a person who was in charge of humanitarian affairs, so of course he was more versed in this than you. He mentioned a road used by military units and by civilians on the Serbian side who were on the territory controlled by the army of Republika Srpska going from point I to point L, all around that red line which we have on this map. So yourself, have you ever heard about this "Salvation Road"? I believe it was called "Salvation Road" or "Road of Life" by the Serbians.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: If Mr. Harland is right, a road of this nature, would that represent a military necessity that must be defended?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be an important road for the Serbian army to get across. That much I would agree with.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking if we could please tender this map and get a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D45, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now if we could have the blank map again on the screen, and zooming in slightly, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So, General, yesterday, when the Prosecutor was asking you questions you talked about elevations and you discussed the elevations that can be seen on this map; some being on territory controlled by the BiH army and others on the territory controlled by the army of Republika Srpska. Do you remember having discussed these elevations?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: We talked about Debelo Brdo. Could you please place a cross, an X, where Debelo Brdo is located.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you talked about the location and there was a superimposition, if I could say so, of several units. So UNPROFOR and both warring parties were located on that elevation at different heights. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the Serbs were just to the south and the Muslims were just below where the UN position was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In yesterday's transcript this is not extremely clear, which is why I'm going back to the same question. Did Serbs occupy Debelo Brdo? That's my first question.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Then, when you talked about the location of the army of Republika Srpska, did you think about another elevation that could have been occupied by this army around Debelo Brdo? There was a superimposition.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I remember was that the UN had the best piece of ground there because they were right on the very top. And the Muslims were just down below and the Serbs were just down to the -- you know, on the southern part of the -- of that map. It was an important piece of ground. Everybody wanted it, and quite frankly, the UN had the best piece of ground there to keep -- but it was something that both sides really wanted to get.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree -- I hope that we can all see that elevation all together. But the slope occupied by the BiH units and the height all the way to the place occupied by the UNPROFOR, all this gives a good vision of the city of Sarajevo. You can really -- it overlooks the city, the city as a whole. Yesterday, you talked about "Sniper Alley," for example. So on that slope there is a good vision of it.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, pretty good. It's a long ways away, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, let's go back to the elevation occupied by the Serbs that was close to Debelo Brdo. Do you remember the name of that other elevation?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Would it refresh your memory if I said Zlatiste?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I can't remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: It doesn't really matter. The name doesn't really matter. Could you describe the geographical position of that other elevation that you talked about yesterday? Where was it located in relation to Debelo Brdo? This was an elevation that was occupied by the Serbian units close to Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I recall were positions that the Serbs occupied, which was a ridge line, that had good observation down into the city. And it was along the southern red line delineating where the Serb position was, going off to the east.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree on the fact that it's even further away from the city centre than Debelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Does the name Vidikovac ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are names that are just -- they're not in my memory right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will need that map for the time being, because we haven't shown much. Let's have a clean version of that map again. Could we zoom in to the part where the 101st Brigade is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: General, can you see the Mojmilo mount on this map? Yesterday, you put a cross on the map. This mount is, in fact, a ridge, a ridge line, quite a long one. Could you please draw a line to indicate Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the time when you went to Lukavica? Do you remember that there was a mount overlooking Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Anyway, yesterday you said that, to your knowledge, Mojmilo mount, whatever its size, was occupied by the units of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in Bosnian control.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We won't need to keep this marking on the map. I would like, once again, to have the clean version of the map, please. Could we zoom in on the part where the marking "105th Brigade" is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: General, yesterday we mentioned Sedrenik; do you remember? And could you please put an X on Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I recall, it's around here. Oh, pardon me. There it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we erase the first X, please. The first one.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And next to the X could you please put an S.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, Sharpstone/Spicasta Stijena, was it close to Sedrenik? Could you please indicate it on the map.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My memory would say it's around this area up here. It's in the north.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please put an S -- well, not an S, I guess. This is Spicasta Stijena, or Sharpstone. This is located inside the blue line; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what my memory is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In any case, in this part of town, the lines between both warring factions were quite close. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were very close.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to retain this map with the markings on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be admitted as Exhibit D46, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I just ask what this small "bb" means. We have a bigger "bbr," which I think is brigade, and then a smaller "bb" in several places.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be a battalion. So in the hierarchy of organisations in the army, you'd have a corps, you'd have a brigade, you'd have a battalion, you'd have a company, a platoon, and then a section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: General, could you then clarify, just to follow up on Judge Robinson's question, in the middle of the map here we see "105.BBR." Would that would be the 105th Bosnian Brigade that had its -- that was placed there? And where was its headquarters? Is that the flags or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, just reading the map, that would be the 105th Brigade's area. It appears that there were a number of battalions. Inferring from the map, the headquarters would -- I'm assessing, are those flags, is where those headquarters would be. But I can't read Bosnian map symbols. And my knowledge doesn't go down to battalion headquarters or brigade headquarters because we didn't visit them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So can you help us explain what do the flags and the double flags symbolise? And the square flags -- triangular flags and square flags.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't answer that question, because I don't know. But where the flags are, given where the battalions are, my assessment would be that that would be the battalion headquarters. So, for example, if you look at "2BB" and you look at the flag - I think it says 2 in there, so I'm guessing right now that that would be the battalion headquarters - and the one to the right of it, it might say a 1. But, again, I can't read these maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: General, just to conclude the examination of this map, there is -- well, there are two symbols where you indicated S. They look like heavy weaponry directed towards the line or something like that. Did you use those symbols in your army as well?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We use similar symbols.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And what do they represent, these two signs, similar to arrows?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They both look like -- the bottom one I think might be a mortar and the top one some sort of Howitzer, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So as a commander, if you put such symbols on the map, does that mean that this heavy weaponry is there?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In theory, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have a matter not related to the proceedings that I have to attend to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wanted to point out to His Honour Judge Harhoff that it's not the Bosnian Brigade. It can only be the 105th Mountain Brigade. It can't be the Bosnian Brigade. I just wanted to explain to Judge Harhoff that it's the 105th Combat Brigade or the Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tapuskovic. Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I just want to register my objection to counsel testifying in the case. If the witness knows the answer and knows what the symbols mean, the witness can testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's perfectly true. Let me hear from the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just a question for Your Worships, should I change my transportation arrangements for this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I will deal with it at the break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Before the Chamber conferred, we had a very interesting question. We were talking about the locations of heavy weaponry. Maybe you could read what is already in the transcript; by this I mean the answers provided by the witness so that I don't have to read them myself, and then I will continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: General, we've put an X on Sedrenik. We've discussed Sedrenik a lot already over the last few days. Do we agree that the symbols representing those heavy weaponry have been placed too close from a residential neighbourhood, i.e., those heavy weaponry was placed too close, according to what you learned in Canada?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't make that conclusion just by where the symbols are on the map. I mean, that's a lot of territory. And there, again, appears to be a lot of open space there, too. So you'd have to see the ground itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe we still have the map on the screen. Can I have the blank map again, please. Could you please enlarge the part where we can read "111th vbbr."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: General, yesterday, the Prosecutor asked you questions about Mount Zuc; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: To your memory, who had control over this mount?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see here, too, the symbols? To your military knowledge, could you tell us what they could represent?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it looks like some sort of Howitzer gun, right beside the "1 bb," and it also looks like some machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please put a Z on Zuc, letter Z, or Z.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: On Zuc.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Where the Howitzers are, is that the place that you identified as being Zuc yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But could you please now put a Z on Zuc, because the Z you have just placed is not on Zuc.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You've also identified another mount, Mount Hum; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please, then, replace your first Z by an H, please.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who was in control on that particular elevation?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslims had control over this whole area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me to say that all this territory between Z and H has a lot of elevations, mounts?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very hilly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And were all those mounts, hills or mounts - because Zuc and Hum are quite high, according to what we can see on the map - are they all oriented towards a part of territory which is not as hilly, as high? I'm talking about the territory controlled by the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just remember these two areas were dominating in this region. I can't really recall what the area to the north-west was looking at, like, where the Serb position was. I think it was actually a little bit lower.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this annotated map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D47, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Let's now move on to another matter, namely, sniping. I would like my case manager to pull up the photograph P201. This exhibit was admitted into evidence yesterday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you talked about a sniper's nest that you were able to visit with General Gobillard in the spring of 1995.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember where --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, we have to wait for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So let's go back to that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: We agreed to say that here we have a sniper's nest that you visited with General Gobillard in the spring of 1995. So, General, if you remember, could you show us, where is the line separating the territory controlled by the BiH army and the territory occupied by the other army on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The red line indicates on this -- the bottom half of the slide would be the Muslim side and the top half would the Serbian side. It's the best way to describe it off this map. That red line actually delineates the river. Muslims were north of the river and Serbs were south of river.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So the river Miljacka is the line, and it separates the two warring factions. But the three high-rises that we see and that are closest to us, do you see those four sky-scrapers? The line is actually going through those sky-skrapers or high-rises. Do you see them?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the four high-rises. They are actually north of the river. In fact, there's another little one that's just behind them, and the line -- don't look at the line because the line is supposed to follow the line, as I was asked yesterday, where the river was. But I see the four high-rises.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'll ask a question to the registrar. We have been taught in e-court, so is it possible to make markings on this very picture?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May markings be made?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that's possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: The original, since -- will it be saved in its current form? Because this is a Prosecution exhibit, as it is now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just for clarification, the parties have the option of either bringing up the original image with no markings and making markings on it or bringing up an image that has already been marked, making additional markings and tendering that exhibit which will contain the original markings and any additional markings that have been made.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I would respectfully ask, since this is a Prosecution exhibit that the Defence now seeks to alter, that we start -- I mean, there's only two marks on it. We could start over fresh, because I'd like the Prosecution exhibit, which was introduced to illustrate a particular point, left the way it is. If that can be done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's fair enough. Did you understand that, Ms. Isailovic? You should introduce your own exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I thought --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can't it be done technologically? Can she not have access to the same but without the markings?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The parties can access the original image with no markings by referring to the original exhibit number, if it's been admitted; and if it hasn't been admitted, the original 65 ter number can be referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty can assist there now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, fine. The 65 ter number is 2819. While it's being pulled up, there's a technical question I would like to ask the registrar. Can we use two different colours in one single picture? Can we make markings in two different colours? Could the registrar please answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That's what I was going to suggest. And if that's possible, if the Defence could mark in blue, for example, I would have no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, it's much ado about nothing, then. Well, yes, the Defence can mark in blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the whole purpose of the exercise, actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So, General, please, with the blue pen, could you please draw that same line, but please don't draw it in the towers, you know, if you could -- because, of course, the towers are on the other side of the river. So draw the line but don't draw the line through the towers, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Meanwhile, may case manager has pulled up a blank photo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So which one do you want me to -- it's a different photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not the same picture, unfortunately. We'll continue with the photograph that's on the screen, but could we have the other -- the marked one, P201. Could we have P201 on the screen, please, and we'll mark it with the blue pen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, General. We're having a bit of problems with technology. Obviously it's not our strong point.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now we have the photograph on the screen, and with the blue pen, could you please draw a line along the separation line. Could you please draw a blue line along the separation line, the river Miljacka, but not in the towers. Just avoid drawing a line through the towers.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So can we agree that the high-rises are on the territory controlled by the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And the towers are facing that red brick building that you marked with a cross.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them are.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, we took advantage of your military knowledge regarding the possible use of snipers inside cities and the general use of sniping. So first, for today's -- what we're doing today, could we first agree on what sniping is, what the concept of sniping is, so that we all talk about the same thing? When I say "sniper," what exactly comes to mind for you?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: A very specialised, highly skilled shooter who has an excellent field-craft in the ability to move in and out of places without being seen. And his targets are of a particularly high value. And we want to use him to capitalise on his marksmanship and his field-craft to get in and out of positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you're talking about the sniper gun, a sniper rifle, there, again, could we agree on the concept of the sniper rifle, the weapon used by the sniper, by this marksman, would be a sniper rifle. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I have to read the transcript and read my question because that's not exactly what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is the definition of that sniper rifle, of that weapon.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Snipers choose weapons based on distance and what they want to try to accomplish. Most sniper rifles have telescopic scopes on them and they can use different calibres to decide what they want to do; heavier calibres for longer ranges and maybe lighter calibres for getting in close, just being able to move the thing back and forth. Snipers pick and choose all sorts of different weapons based on what they have to do. For example, the French had principally two sniper rifles for their snipers. They had a .50 calibre Beretta, very, very large, and then they also had a -- I think it was a 7.62-millimetre rifle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, we're going to take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please continue. I should said to both parties that I'm not satisfied with the progress being made in the trial. When time-limits are set, they should be complied with. The estimates of time have been -- some of them have been quite out. In one case we had two hours as the estimate and the examination-in-chief was six hours and 40 minutes. The estimates that we have made for the duration of the case have been based on those times that have been given to us. So I expect more rigour and discipline from both parties, and there's no better person to begin with than the Defence. So that's what I have to say to you, Ms. Isailovic. Let's have rigour and discipline and focus in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that the time that the Defence will have has to do with the time that the in-chief took. See, according to what has happened during the in-chief, you know, I prepare my own cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Generally, Ms. Isailovic and Mr. Tapuskovic, you have had more time than the Prosecution. I asked for a breakdown and it shows that the Defence have spent more time in cross-examination than the Prosecution, and fairly significantly more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was recently a witness that was examined by the Prosecution for three days. I managed to cross him in one day, although I could have used more. We are really doing our best for that purpose. A recent Prosecution witness testified in chief for three days and my cross-examination took only one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I did refer to that case as six hours and 40 minutes spent in examination-in-chief. How much time did the Prosecution spend, Mr. Court Deputy, for examination-in-chief of this witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's proceed, and just tell me how much time Ms. Isailovic has spent. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Just before I resume, I believe that the count of time can be explained by Rule 92 ter. In this rule, you know, the Prosecution can present, as evidence, some statements that we spent some time on earlier, and I believe the time we use there, of course, must be longer than the time used by Prosecution for the 92 ter witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that is perfectly true, because they are really using the shorter and abbreviated method of presenting. So I take that into account. But I can assure you that I will not stand by or sit and have any unfairness or injustice done to the Defence. I value cross-examination, but it must be pointed, it must be relevant, you know, and focused. Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to our photograph that's in front of us. Could you please look at the building on which you placed a cross. Am I right to say that this building is very close to the confrontation line separating the two warring factions?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: General, in urban conditions, so when war is being made within a densely populated area, with a lot of buildings, do the buildings located on the borderline, about the same thing as what trenches would represent in a meadow or in a field?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every one of those buildings in that picture represents a trench. Every one.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is it legitimate for the party defending the territory located behind that trench, represented by a building, isn't it legitimate for that party to defend its territory and to use this building, for example, as a place where it would station weapons?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to what you remember regarding that sniper's nest. You talked about holes that had been made in the walls, spider holes.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. There were little holes that were knocked through the wall.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: There were also sandbags.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: According to your military knowledge, what could these sandbags be used for?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could be used for shoring up holes, acting as protective measures, or they could also be used as supports to rest weapons or yourself on. Multiple uses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Those holes that you noted when you were touring that building with General Gobillard, would they be identical if you want to place weapons that have an optical sight or weapons that don't have an optical sight? Would they be the same holes?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A hole is a hole. You can point anything out of it, with or without a scope.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that there is no cause and effect relationship between finding a hole and knowing that a sniper is going to be used, a sniper as we defined it today?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Having a hole doesn't indicate that a sniper used it; it just indicates a potential position where somebody with a rifle could use and fire from.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: A plain shooter, who would be a member of one of the units of the Republika Srpska army, if he wanted to shoot using a simple rifle would use that same hole.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: To put it another way, the fact that there are those holes and that those sandbags were there does not necessarily imply that marksmen were using that spot.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It just implies that somebody was using that spot for something other than what it was designed for, because a hole, spider hole, has a military purpose, to either go through or shoot through, and sandbags are normally designed to help defenders to use that position, to enhance it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you're saying to make those shots more effective, you're talking about the shots fired by a rifle or the shots made with a sniper, sniper rifle, as we said today?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not make much difference between a rifle and a sniper rifle because it has the same effect when you fire it against a target. Sandbags, in positions that I saw, would make it easier for somebody who want to the fire a rifle to fire at a target.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Earlier we talked about the buildings on the confrontation line and we said they could be assimilated to trenches in a field. Now I'd like to ask you questions about the shots themselves and their impact on a particular item that is taken as the target. Are there differences to be noticed on the target of a specific shot? Are there differences according to the type of rifle that's being used, i.e., a plain rifle, on the one hand, and a rifle with a sight?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The impact on a target -- if you shoot a soldier, there is a certain effect in impact. If you shoot a civilian, there's a different impact. And there is more of a psychological impact shooting a civilian than there is -- if that's how I understand your question. No? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was talking about the physical, the impact created by a bullet when a bullet hits a particular object or a person, which is of course a tragic event, but that happened. Can you make a difference and determine whether the bullet was shot with a simple rifle or with a sniper rifle?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: By examination of whatever was hit by the round, you can determine what kind of rifle fired it. You can't say whether or not it was a sniper rifle or not, because the rifle is the same in a lot of cases. The scope just gives you better accuracy. But having watched soldiers fire for 26 years, there are some exceptionally good shots, people who can fire rifles without a scope. It's a function of distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, let's go back to the photograph. We have the four towers just opposite the line, the separation line, i.e., the Miljacka river. Do you think that these towers would offer a good position towards the units that are deployed on the other side of the river defending the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those would be potentially good positions for the other side.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Let's take an example, and here I'm trying to take advantage of your knowledge and experience. If there was a shooting between both sides, i.e., between the towers and the buildings on the opposite side, could it be that the civilian targets which would be stuck in the middle could be hit but unintentionally, of course?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible but unlikely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Why are you saying "unlikely"?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're talking about snipers, snipers are skilled marksmen. They will take some time and care to line up the target, and, assuming that the target is a military target, it is it unlikely that they will miss. That's why they are called snipers and that's why they are as good as they are. And even a rifleman, based on my experience, is normally proficient in the firing of their weapon, and before they fire their weapon, they do go through that shoot criteria that I said yesterday. And if there is a doubt about possibly hitting a civilian -- and I've seen soldiers, even in Sarajevo, not take the shot if they thought there was a doubt about hitting somebody they didn't want to hit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: General, in a space such as the one that is shown in this picture, is it very likely that a bullet could make a ricochet?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ricochets are very possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to turn to my case manager so that she pulls up 65 ter document 2819 on the screen. My apologies. I'd like to tender that photograph into evidence and I would like an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D48, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's now move on to the next photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: General, this picture shows a different view. I'm sure you're familiar with what's depicted on this picture, because we're going to have a look at the Holiday Inn hotel area. First of all, could you tell us where the confrontation or separation line was between the two warring factions, please. Could you indicate it?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It follows along the river. I won't draw through the buildings, but if you follow the red line, it goes behind that building. You see that line goes behind the building and, again, just follows along.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, General, could you indicate on this picture what you called yesterday "Sniper's Alley."

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me to say that in between the confrontation line and "Sniper's Alley" there's a stretch of land quite heavily built, this being part of the territory controlled by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, the towers dominating in the background, are you in a position to identify those towers and tell us what their name was?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two towers, I think they were called the Unis towers. The Holiday Inn, we talked about. And I can't remember what this tower was called.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the building of the assembly?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was that one right there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This tower located, let's say, between the assembly and the Holiday Inn, do you know -- yes, this one. Do you know what its purpose was?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to keep that photograph with its markings, knowing that I will go to back to this photograph eventually. But, first of, all I would like to show to the witness parts of the statement he gave in 1997. Could we have an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be admitted as Exhibit D49, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask my case manager to bring up Exhibit DD00-0522. Let's move on to page 11 -- no, before that, let's have a look at page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is the first page of your statement. Do you remember the time when you gave that statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have look at page 11. I do have to apologise because we didn't find this declaration in e-court, so we had to photocopy my own copy. Please ignore the numbers. I have numbered a few paragraphs and I have put the number 72.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please re-read that part and I will ask a few questions.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, let's leave that statement aside for a moment, and let's go back to the photograph with its markings, which has now become D49. General, you have had the opportunity to read your statement. Do you still confirm what is in it?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like you to show the buildings you've identified in your statement as being buildings used by the ABiH as sniping positions?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said in the statement earlier, we had gotten reports of them using the assembly building and the Unis towers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be possible to place circles around A and U with the blue pen, please.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: General, would you agree with me to say that those two buildings and the way they were used during the conflict give a good position and a good view over "Sniper's Alley"? This is the name that you use yourself.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're good positions, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And as regards civilians and tramways, are these good positions to shoot on, on these targets?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: During your period of service in Sarajevo, did your investigations show that there were other snipers' positions along this street, Zmaja od Bosne, that you called "Sniper's Alley"?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for whose side are we talking about now? Are we talking about the north side of the river or the south side of the river?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the north side of the river.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Potentially, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you possibly remember those positions, locations?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, any building. By the same token, we had no information that -- as I said yesterday, I only knew of one case where allegedly the Muslims were firing at their own people, and I didn't hear of anything else along "Sniper's Alley" of positions that they would be using against that road. But the buildings themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But, of course, on the other hand, you cannot exclude that other buildings may have been used as snipers' positions.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's tender this photograph into evidence first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D50, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like my case manager to pull up on the screen 65 ter document number 1904. My apologies. This is not the right document. It should be 65 ter document 1917.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, if you remember, Mr. Prosecutor showed you this document.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember seeing that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: General, do you remember the date or the time when General Milosevic was first referred to as the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, approximately?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it was very early on in my tour, but I can't remember the exact date. But I still recall that he was also part of the corps previous to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But you don't remember the exact date when he took his function of corps commander.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly. It might been the May/June period, but I don't know. I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the date of this document is June 25th, 1994?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And will you agree with me, too, that on the first page of that document - and I'd like you to read what is written here and then I will ask you a few questions - the activities of snipers from both sides are or have increased, mainly on the southern and western areas of Sarajevo. And then we talk about Grbavica and a few other places as well.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And then after this, the document continues with a figure, average number, the average number being ten per week, including civilians and military.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: That the situation may lead to an escalation.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: The date of this document is June 25th, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the exhibit 65 ter 1973 to be shown. This is document 1973, a 65 ter document which was admitted into evidence as Prosecution Exhibit 206. Here it is. This is the Anti-Sniping Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Please read the date of this document.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's dated the 14th of August, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at the signatures on this document. Can you read them?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is signed by Karavelic, Milosevic, Rose and Viktor Andreev. And they date it the 14th of August, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, once again, I'd like to take advantage of the knowledge gathered during your stay in Sarajevo, and I would like to you explain to us something about this agreement. This is an agreement in which some notions or concepts are used, and after this agreement has been signed, it is then interpreted to be implemented; and in doing so, of course, one has to remember what the parties were aiming at when they did conclude that agreement. Now, what's interesting for me in this particular agreement is the notion of "sniper."

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, it's the notion of sniping activities, which is not a sniper. It's slightly different.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: General, to your memory, what was the purpose of this agreement? Was the aim to suppress all shots coming from the sniper rifles, from all rifles in general, or all the shooting coming from sniper rifles?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The intent behind this agreement was to get both parties to stop shooting at each other, sniping, which was inclusive of snipers but not just exclusive -- it didn't exclude everyone else. Anybody who was firing at those targets, the intent here was to have everybody stop shooting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise for interrupting Ms. Isailovic's cross-examination. I'm just looking at the time. I know that General Fraser was very keen to be able to travel back to Canada and not be held over the weekend. I don't know if that's possible. I can tell the Court that right now I have no re-examination, based on what I have heard so far. I don't know if Judge Mindua has to go to the other trial this afternoon. I know this courtroom is empty. The Prosecution is willing to sit longer if it will help General Fraser get out of here this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Isailovic, how much longer do you intend to be?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, I have many issues to discuss with this witness who is, for me, very important for the Chamber. I'm facing quite an uncomfortable situation, because when I started my cross-examination -- well, I started it and then have I'll have to stop it, but, of course, I do understand the desire expressed by the General. Maybe Mr. Docherty could have thought about this issue a bit earlier on. In this case, I could have adjusted my cross-examination to the duration of the examination-in-chief. So here, in fact, I'm being faced with quite an uncomfortable situation. I would have loved to accede to the General's desire, but on the other hand, of course, what is at heart here, as far as I'm concerned, is to defend my client's interests. I'd rather favour the interests of the defence of General Milosevic in this case

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When was the General planning to travel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My flight was scheduled for 3.30 this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't think you'll make that. You won't make that. It's 25 past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We're pretty close to when I ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And when is the next flight? It's tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The staff would have to find me another flight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, you are an important witness. The evidence is important to the Defence. But I still want to know how much longer you plan to be, Ms. Isailovic. I wouldn't like you to think that you can go on and on and on and on. That will not be permitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: No. I just wanted to use the same time that was used by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh, you're well beyond that time. You're well beyond that time. So don't take that course. But I don't apply those times mechanically, so tell us how much longer you will be.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, I need to finish on the issue of sniping, a few questions, a document, and then a few questions; and then I wanted to discuss two matters. But then it is up to you to decide, and I will abide by your decision. But I don't think that I have used more time than the Prosecutor for that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, you have. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Time flies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, you have, because the direct was an hour and 58 minutes, and when we came back this afternoon you had already done an hour and 44 minutes, when we came back from the last break. I believe we are in a position to go beyond the scheduled time for the adjournment at 1.45, because I have been involved in a decision which would have the staff leave at 2.00, all staff. So if the staff here can stay for, say, another half an hour, we could go to a quarter past 2.00, at the latest.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'd like my case manager to pull up 65 ter document 0211 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I just make it clear that you are not to utilise the time if you don't have to. I was just setting that as an outside limit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood. Let's have a look at page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: General, please, this is a document you saw with the Prosecutor yesterday. "Assessment of the Results." This assessment was made on September 15th, 1994, one month after the enforcement of the Anti-Sniping Agreement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So now could you please read what's on the screen. It's an assessment. On the second paragraph, it says that the ideal situation would be to have no shots whatsoever, to reach the figure zero, but there are a few reasons to show that it would be impossible. And in the line it says "because of provocation shots," that's in one of the bullet, [In English] "and lost bullets increasing the confrontation line close to inhabited areas." [Interpretation] So we agree that there was a problem of lost bullets throughout the conflict. Do we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'll now quickly move on to another question. Yesterday, we talked about the anti-sniping task force; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement -- maybe we could take a look at it. This is document DD00-0522. On page 14, please, paragraph 94, could you please read it quickly. You're talking about a problem regarding the investigations made by UNMOs. They weren't quite reliable regarding your sector anyway. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: UNMOs varied depending on which country you were dealing with. Overall this sector did not rely on UNMOs. We used our own soldiers and units to do the investigations where we could.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So after obtaining information, did your sector make its own report on a very specific incident? Did you make your own report?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sector was fairly rigorous in making reports on anything that it investigated. The French were very good. They would always write up a report and that would be passed up to the appropriate authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, if we could take a look at document DD00-0581. The first page, please. I wanted to show you a report on an investigation made by the sector and by UNMOs, but we're having problems.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document I have in e-court, DD00-0581, is three pages but all three pages are blank.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we did what we were supposed to do to have it on e-court. Let's move to document DD00-0575, please. The document is in French.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is that a problem for you?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me read it and I'll tell you if it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: These two documents, the one that unfortunately was not uploaded and this other one, were a combination. Could you tell us the nature of this document we have here on the screen in French.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be a summary of an incident that happened on the 4th of September. Sharpe seems to be reporting. And it is a chronological event from 10.37 to 10.45, what happened. It looks like two shots were fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could we agree to say that the figures here are the time? 10.37, 10.40, that's the time; right?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. That is the time when actions were taking place there, and it was explained what actions took place at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please take a look at page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And 1930, 7.30 p.m., can you read what is written at 1930.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it says that they had contact with the liaison information officer from the 105th Brigade, BiH. They declared -- it was on the position occupied by Dacoy, saying that after the investigation ...

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then in the next paragraph it says that -- what does it say, according to where the shots originated from?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it says that a Bravo 50 machine-gun fired on a BSA position located at Orlovac, 93256250. I think that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, if we could take a look now at page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Read what happened at 3.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's a -- correct me if I'm wrong, but I think they identified a group of three buildings 200 metres to the north. They're just identifying where they thought the shots came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: The name Breka, does it ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, the point -- it would become -- firstly, if it could be shown on the document we tried to have, and it couldn't be uploaded. But I have it as a hard copy. We'll ask for a number for this document, please, just so that I can tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, which document was that?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Document DD00-0575.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be admitted as Exhibit D51, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One last question regarding sniping. If we could please call up document 65 ter 428. While it is being displayed, I will ask a few questions, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: First, this name of Zmaja od Bosne road, the name "Sniper Alley," I'm interested in that. When did you hear that name mentioned for the first time regarding that street, that avenue?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I actually arrived on the ground as part of my handover, they showed me where "Sniper's Alley" was. That's what we called it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you're saying "I was shown." Could you tell us who showed you that and who told you that that was the name of that street?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My predecessor, Christian De Bergeron, when he took me around and showed me the area, and when I was going around with my boss, I mean, that's when I first found out where that route was and what it was called.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you how this name came about, how it was coined, and when it started being used?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was coined because all of the sniping activity that took place along that route. When it was actually coined, that, I don't recall. I don't think he ever told me when it was. It just was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But sniping, when you think about the word "sniping," it's not the only place where it occurred.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, but it happened to be most infamous place where sniping occurred.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: At the time did you know of another route, a safer route that could be used instead of that "Sniper's Alley"?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were other routes that you could take further into town and you could sneak your way through. That route happened to be where the tram -- the tram used that route and that's where people used that route. And we put up a lot of passive barriers along that route and other routes to try to mitigate the potential threat to civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, regarding that route, the fact that the tram was using it, we're interested in this because we have looked at quite a few number of tram incidents. So who decided whether the tram would be running or not? Was it your sector that was in charge of that kind of decision?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Bosnian Muslim authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: General, at the time did you know how decisions were made? Maybe they used to get information from your sector to assess the safety of the time, to see whether it was safe or not to run the tram?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't ever recall them coming to us asking us for advice on running the tram. I do recall that they would make assessments based on their own evaluation and they would complain to us in fact if they were getting too much sniping activity against the trams and asking us to do more. A lot of that would come through either Minister Muratovic or through the Presidency itself, through one of the three key figures, the President, the Vice-Pesident, or the Prime Minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can we conclude from this that the BiH army and the BiH government were controlling whether trams would be running or not?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree to saying that they were a warring faction in that sector on -- at the same time. Simultaneously they were also a warring faction?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were one of the three parties involved in the conflict in Bosnia, yes. They were also just trying to run a city too.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move to a document that we use quite extensively here. It's a Defence exhibit, D41. Could we please pull it up and enlarge it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: General, could you please help us to try and understand this first -- this cover page. You see it on the screen, please?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was just waiting for the --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Outgoing -- whatever, that's the document that we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a situational report for the period covering 27 February from 0001 Alpha time zone to 1700 Alpha. It is from headquarters UNPROFOR and -- pardon me, yeah, from BH command which was General Rose's headquarters, and it's going to headquarters Zagreb and informing all the sectors. So it has an info addressee block and has an internal addressee block. And in this particular one, three big points were aircraft fired at the airport, four injured people on the tram, shooting in Sarajevo, a UN convoy was fired at at Srebrenica, and then it goes into a general assessment. Standard situation report.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But what I'm interested in now is how these reports were actually drafted. In Sarajevo you had a sector. There was the BH command and the UNMO command. So did all three groups take place in drafting such reports? Did all three groups actually provide information in order to compile that report for that very day. Is that how it worked?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody in the chain of command was responsible for meeting information requirements for their higher headquarters. Simplistically we would -- the force commander up in Zagreb would be asking for a report at a certain time per day that would cover a certain period of time. General Rose or Smith would have to comply with that, and they would put in the information that the force commander was looking for and what also transpired during that day. In turn, my headquarters would have to reply to that, to give them the information that they needed to fill that report out for the force commander and for the Bosnia-Herzegovina commander, read Rose and Smith. It was a -- it was a big pyramid series of reports and returns that meets not only your commander's requirement but the requirements of your higher and telling people what was going on during the day. In this particular case, three major incidents were reported that were shown right there at the message.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So this document is 23 pages long. If you could please help us understand how it's organised. So can we please move on to page 2. It starts with an assessment. And then paragraph 3 it says "faction activity." And, for example, regarding the tram. After that figure 8, could you please read that passage, starting there.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The passage starting at 8. "Eight times small arms rounds were fired at a tram near Holiday Inn" - and gives the grid - "injuring four (not confirmed) people. The origin is assessed as being in the Vrbanja bridge/red building area" - gives a grid - "where a fire-fight between both factions occurred at the same time. The tram service was halted. A proposed reconnaissance of the crew pack area was cancelled due to non-cooperation" --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Finish off with the tram. When the sector is being mentioned, Vrbanja bridge/red building area, and then right after that there's a series of figures. What exactly does this represent?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those figures are map coordinates that help people go to a map and find out where the Holiday Inn is, for example, or where Vrbanja bridge/the red building area is so they can actually see a map and put together the details in this report to a map.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So, those BP -- that BP with those figure, like BP 912589, does this help find a sector or a very specific point on the map?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It helps to find a very specific point. Every map has got both a Alpha and numeric reference. You have to know which maps we're looking at. You go, first of all, to Bravo Papa, and then you go to that grid number. 912 is the first three numbers, they're important, 589, it's called in -- in military jargon it's a six-figure grid reference which will give you an actual point on the ground. Just to help you to visualise what -- where it is we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, one more thing. In the report, we find out that this incident with the tram is on three different places in the report. Because on page 9, for example --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could please move to page 9 and show it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Here after the heading is paragraph 2, Sector Sarajevo. And on the fourth paragraph in Sector Sarajevo, could you please read that again, starting at "a tram travelling." Could you please read it out loud?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: "A tram travelling between BP 910593 and BP 907592, was fired at, reportedly resulting in one confirmed civilian casualty and possibly three other casualties. The confirmed casualty suffered a leg injury. The estimated origin of fire was" -- and it gives where that was. "Tramway service ceased following the incident. During the same time period, both sides were involved in a fire-fight 300 metres away in the area of the Vrbanja bridge," and gives the location, and I think that it says, "machine-gun confirmed has been -- machine-gun was been attributed to both the BiH and BSA for the event overall." I'm not sure what that CFV means. And then it goes to say what happened at 0950. "A few small arms bursts were fired at an aircraft."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. We wanted to obtain your assistance for that "MG" and then "CFV," because I thought that CFV meant cease-fire violation. Am I right in having guessed that?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That's -- that's a good deduction. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And MG?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I read that would be machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So in the report, there's also mention of the weapon that was used. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears from the reading of this that that's what it is saying, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And also, it says [In English] Vrbanja bridge. [Interpretation] So when you're saying -- when it is mentioned like that, is it -- could it be an area that would be wider and broader than just the plain Vrbanja bridge? Is that -- or -- or is it the Vrbanja bridge and only the Vrbanja bridge?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell from reading this report how it transpired from this report. You would have to go down to the report from the next lower level and ask -- and get more details on what happened at that incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but in that same report, this is also mentioned on page 23, and there the UNMOs are mentioned. Paragraph H, please. Paragraph H, as in Hector. Could you scroll down to H? Here this incident is mentioned for a third time. This is made -- compiled from information obtained by UNMOs, and there's quite a discrepancy between what was described on page 2 and what was described on page 9. Discrepancies mainly have to do with the number of shots. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not unusual that in an incident like this when you get multiple people reporting you will get multiple pieces of information, and you'll have to piece it together like a detective to figure out what happened. I think what is clear is one female was hit in the leg and the tram was shot. The number of rounds fire, I mean, it's pretty hard. You have to figure out, you know, visual reports for people coming -- how many rounds did they see, how many holes were in the tram. It's not uncommon that you get a lot of information that's not quite synchronised that you have to piece it together. It's a difficult process.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: My last question regarding this report is the following. There's information on specific evidence in three places. So, according to you, is there one part of the report that takes priority over others or not? Because this could be quite confusing for somebody reading this report. It's hard to understand, and -- so is one part taking priority over the others?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. How the report is normally written is you get the bottom line up front with the bullets of what was important, that the commander who sends out the report wants his commander, his boss above him, to note. The report will then start off with a general overview of the situation in his specific area of responsibility. In this case, the report would have been from -- Bosnia and Herzegovina, the whole country. Then each sector then goes into more and more detail. So the further you get into the report, the more detail you get on incidents and whatnot. And then there is a whole series of routine reports on things as much as -- like, how much fuel you have, how much food you have, just routine matters. So the further you get into it, more and more detail. And a whole bunch -- if you looked at the distribution list, a whole bunch of people read this report and take a whole bunch of things out of it for their own purposes. But its intent is to paint a picture of what is going on, to give enough information, accurate information, so that things like what we talked about earlier for General Rose to go and talk to the people and to say, Look, this is happening, we need to get control over this. And the importance of reports is to get the information up as fast as possible, and sometimes that information is truncated. It's complicated and not completely accurate, and over the days they would have refined this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But overall can we conclude out of this report that there was an exchange of fire and that as a consequence the tram was shot, the consequence of this exchange of fire. Is that something that could be inferred from this report without really going into the details?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also read in the report that, in fact, there appears to almost two things happening here. This was an engagement at a bridge, and there appears to have been some sort of sniping activity on the tram. So we could have actually two incidents actually being reported in one paragraph. That's how I'm -- I'm actually inferring from this report. So if the allegation is did the shooting from the Vrbanja bridge actually hit the tram, I'm reading something else here. I'm reading the report the tram was actually specifically targeted, from what the words are saying here, "sniper fire against a tram." That is a very deliberate, definite action. That's what it says there, and that's what I would take away from that paragraph H.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So out of this report, do you read that it was deliberate, a deliberate action?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I read from this is, is it appears from paragraph H the tram was sniped at.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But of the two other paragraphs, could you be as sure? Because as I said earlier, the -- if incidents is related in those three places in the report, so are the two others as sure?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from the earlier paragraph, it -- all it was was a statement that there was a fight going on at the Vrbanja bridge. There was no direct correlation made from there that the fighting there actually impacted on the tram. In fact, this tells me, gives me for detail from that to say I think there were two things happening in the same time period; a fight at Vrbanja, and sniping against a tram. That's what I'm getting out of this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can we look at page 2 again, please, then. Page 1 -- A, paragraph A. Sector Sarajevo, paragraph A. Out of this paragraph, out of this report ...

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, having read the more details, again I would infer from this that while there might have been fighting going on at Vrbanja bridge, someone in this area might have directly targeted and sniped at the tram at the same time. Because it -- again, it's -- when I put those two pieces together, that's kind of the picture I'm getting when I read this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have just been informed that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If that is so, then I owe Judge Mindua an apology. He will have no break whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: It's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just five minutes. Five minutes -- five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise in advance. Everybody is going to hate me. But one last question. Could you pull document DD00-0573. Your Honour, this is an order from the commander of the 1st Corps of the BiH army. Unfortunately, we have no translation in English. But maybe the interpreters could help us. All I need is the translation of two sentences in this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, can that be translated.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. So today we did mention a few personalities, Mr. Karavelic, for example. He was the commander of the 1st Corps of the BiH army. And could you please read the following sentence? I will read it, actually. The heading is: "Treatment of UNPROFOR forces. UNPROFOR forces are to be treated in the following manner. The units being infiltrated into the demilitarised zone through the 20-kilometre exclusion zone past the UNPROFOR forces are to be taken in full secrecy. The bringing in and the deployment of units is to be covered up and camouflaged. Units attacking from the front lines in the exclusion zone and in the UNPA zone, in accordance with the agreement dated the 13th of August, 1993, in the stage of being brought in, in the approach stage and the stage when they come into contact, should also take measures to cover up this activity until the units are brought" --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Have you heard this? And could you read the date that is written on this document. If we could scroll up a little. Scroll -- scroll the other way around, please. Scroll up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This is the last question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: The date, please?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: 30th of the 9th, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So here comes my last question. Do you remember an event that occurred on October 6th, 1994, when the units of the BH army going through the safe area actually slaughtered 19 members of a health corps belonging to the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall the incident. I also -- my understanding was it was not a completely -- it wasn't a complete health unit. In fact, it was a Serbian headquarters that had a health staff attached to it, and it was a violent attack. I do recall that. I do recall that -- in fact, I think it was the Serbian corps had asked us to go and try to find one individual, a female, who was not accounted for. We went back to General Karavelic and asked him if he knew about the whereabouts of this one person that was unaccounted for, and he did not know and -- but he said he would look. We never did find out what happened to that female.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We must stop now. Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Brigadier, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for giving it and you may now leave. In any event, we will be adjourning now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 12th day of February, 2007, at 9.00 p.m. 23 24 25
